## 3. Numbers in the cover-letter claims and the summary that are not values in results.json

None.

Design constants and counts that are written in the sentences (ranges, seeds, thresholds, family sizes) are skipped by the filter; every other number must match a results.json value to the rounding shown.

## 4. Origin labels of the finishing keys

Every f.* key carries a label allowed for its block (simulation blocks are never MEASURED_SOFTWARE; the B-block collision and airtime checks are ANALYTICAL or SIMULATED).

Count of f.* keys by label: MEASURED_SOFTWARE 621, SIMULATED 9733, ANALYTICAL 81, NOT_RUN 17

## 5. Claims stronger than their label (read by the author)

- The cover-letter claims name the label of each claim. Simulated results are phrased as statements under stated assumptions. The synthetic results are called a stress test. No sentence claims a field, hardware or real-crash result.
- Where an earlier document (`docs/03_results/CLAIM_EVIDENCE.md`, `docs/archive/CLAIMS_FOR_COVER_LETTER_V1.md`) states a licence as not stated, it is superseded by `docs/05_data_code/DATA_AND_CODE_STATEMENT.md` (changed in A1).
